title: DRIVE OUT WHAT WOULD DESTROY YOU

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho the Lord said to Moses, "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'When you cross the Jordan into Canaan, drive out all the inhabitants of the land before you. Destroy all their carved images and their cast idols, and demolish all their high places. Take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess.'" - Num 33:50-53 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now God gives clear instructions for entering the land. Central to them is a firm command: drive out the inhabitants and destroy every idol, every carved image, every high place of false worship. This was not about cruelty; it was about protecting Israel from the very thing that had already nearly destroyed them — the pull toward idolatry and unfaithfulness to God. The Canaanite religion was steeped in practices God abhorred, and mixing with it would corrupt His people's hearts.

We must keep this command in its own covenant-historical setting; it was a specific instruction to Israel at a unique moment, not a pattern for the church to imitate against people today. Jesus makes clear that His kingdom does not advance by force against others (John 18:36).

But the underlying spiritual principle speaks powerfully to us. God calls His people to deal decisively with the idols in our own lives. We are not called to drive out nations, but we are called to demolish whatever competes with God for the throne of our hearts. Half-measures with sin and idolatry do not work; what we tolerate, we eventually serve.

Whatever functions as an idol for you — money, approval, comfort, a relationship, a habit — God lovingly calls you to tear down its "high places" in your heart. This is not to rob you of joy but to free you for wholehearted devotion to Him. In Christ we have the power to put sin to death by the Spirit (Rom 8:13). Do not negotiate with your idols. Demolish them, and take possession of the freedom God gives.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "idols" or high places has God called you to tear down in your heart?
2. Where are you tempted to make half-measures with sin instead of dealing decisively?
3. How does the Spirit's power free you to put these things to death?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, show me the idols hidden in my heart, and give me courage to tear them down. By Your Spirit, free me for wholehearted devotion to You alone. Amen.
